title: Crash in nsHttpChannel::ContinueProcessResponse1 and ContinueProcessResponse3 on null mAuthProvider
body: I found a new Firefox release crash signature through the crash spike detector. The crash is an EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION_READ in mozilla::net::nsHttpChannel::ContinueProcessResponse1; a similar ContinueProcessResponse3 signature may be the same issue. Looking at several reports, the crash occurs at `rv = mAuthProvider->CheckForSuperfluousAuth();`, so `mAuthProvider` may be null. This appears to be a possible release crash regression.

symptoms_visible: Firefox release crashes with EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION_READ in nsHttpChannel::ContinueProcessResponse1; another group of reports crashes in ContinueProcessResponse3.
N0.label: N0 release crash spike reported

symptoms_visible: Firefox starts crashing after restart when my Autoconfig includes an invalid autoadmin.global_config_url; removing that line lets it start.
Other reports say Firefox 128 crashes when a proxy is configured or after saved proxy authentication is reused.
N1.label: N1 proxy and Autoconfig conditions surfaced

symptoms_visible: Firefox still crashes with network.auth.use_redirect_for_retries set to false.
When I tried setting the preference to true, Firefox crashed and the preference was false again afterward.
N2.label: N2 redirect preference probe completed

symptoms_visible: The affected Firefox installation continues to crash with the invalid global configuration URL enabled.
N3.label: N3 HTTP log collected

symptoms_visible: Firefox 128.0.2 no longer crashes with the affected configuration.
N_terminal.label: terminal crash prevented in updated build

question_patterns: Do the affected installations have any enterprise Autoconfig settings, and can you identify a setting that makes the crash reproducible?
What configuration is present when Firefox starts crashing?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On my installation, the difference is this line in `mozilla.cfg`: `lockPref("autoadmin.global_config_url", "http://internal-server/invalid-url/firefox.js");`. If I remove it Firefox works; if I put it back and restart Firefox twice, it starts crashing again.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The crashes occur on an unmanaged installation with no Autoconfig, proxy, PAC file, or authentication settings.
The invalid global configuration URL uses HTTPS instead of HTTP, but enabling it produces the same crash.

question_patterns: Is Firefox using a proxy or an automatic proxy configuration script?
What proxy mode is selected on the affected machine?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Firefox is forced to use the system proxy configuration. Windows Internet Settings downloads a 51 KB `config.pac` file from the automatic configuration script setting before Firefox crashes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Firefox is set to No proxy, and there is no system or PAC configuration.

edges.comment: Comments 4-7 are folded into one simulated user side. An affected administrator supplied the invalid Autoconfig URL and PAC reproduction, while the original reporter supplied proxy-authentication comments found in other crash reports.

question_patterns: Can you set network.auth.use_redirect_for_retries to false and report whether Firefox still crashes?
Please check the value of network.auth.use_redirect_for_retries and test the crashing setup with it disabled.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It was already false, and Firefox still crashed. I created crash report `3530d9e0-be3f-4a11-a143-ce0940240722` with it set to false.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Setting network.auth.use_redirect_for_retries to false stops the crashes across restarts.
It is false and the same crash occurs, but the resulting crash report has a different ID.

question_patterns: What happens if you test the same setup with network.auth.use_redirect_for_retries set to true?
Does the preference remain set after the crash and restart?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried setting it to true and got crash report `754f3d8b-c383-4900-9c92-c2ffa0240722`, but after reporting the crash I noticed the option was false again.

edges.comment: This is a handler-initiated configuration probe, so it is modeled as a measurement clarification. Its raw result rules out treating the proposed pref flip as the established fix.

question_patterns: Could you capture an HTTP log with logging to a file while reproducing the crash and send it to the Necko team?
Please collect a file-based HTTP log from an affected machine.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Log sent. It is from the first PC, the one associated with crash report `d8da664a-8543-4bb6-87c5-482a50240722`; the two preference-test crash reports came from a second PC.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I sent the same log from the first PC under a different email subject.

edges.comment: The user reports only that the requested log was captured and sent, plus which machine it came from. No engineer interpretation of the private log is placed in the user's answer.

question_patterns: Please retest in Firefox 128.0.2 and tell me whether it still crashes with the same configuration.
Can you reproduce the startup crash in the current updated build?

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Firefox 128.0.2 still crashes with the same invalid global configuration URL and system proxy setup.

solution.intent: Prevent the two nsHttpChannel response-processing crashes by checking mAuthProvider before dereferencing it and aborting response processing when it is null, while explicitly treating this as crash containment because the reason the provider becomes null remains unknown.
solution.concrete_example: Add null checks for `mAuthProvider` in the affected ContinueProcessResponse paths and return early rather than calling authentication methods through a null pointer. The patch shipped in Firefox 128.0.2 and related maintained branches, but it is a workaround to stop the crash; the underlying reason `mAuthProvider` becomes null was not determined in this bug.
solution.inference_hint: The known immediate failure is a null dereference of mAuthProvider in the response-processing paths. The proxy, PAC, invalid global configuration URL, and saved-authentication reports establish triggering conditions, but the thread never determines why mAuthProvider becomes null. The landed null checks are therefore containment rather than a proven correction of the underlying state transition.

edges.comment: The null-check patch landed before the affected user installed Firefox 128.0.2. The retest is terminal-side verification and is deliberately excluded from the solution's required_info.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the established immediate crash cause: nsHttpChannel dereferences a null mAuthProvider in the ContinueProcessResponse1 and ContinueProcessResponse3 response-processing paths.

Must ground the diagnosis in the crash line and collected configuration evidence, including the proxy/Autoconfig correlation and the fact that network.auth.use_redirect_for_retries=false still crashes.
Must recommend the actual containment fix: null-check mAuthProvider and abort or return before calling through it in both affected response paths.
Must not claim that changing network.auth.use_redirect_for_retries to false fixes the issue; the affected installation already had it false and still crashed.
Must not overstate bug 1741375, proxy DNS behavior, the invalid global configuration URL, or the PAC file as the proven root mechanism; the reason mAuthProvider becomes null remained unknown.
Must ask the user to verify on an updated build and treat the issue as resolved only after the user reports that Firefox 128.0.2 no longer crashes.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical crash triager combined with an affected enterprise-config user: comfortable reading crash stacks and source code, comparing crash signatures, editing mozilla.cfg and about:config, and collecting HTTP logs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise and evidence-driven; supplies exact crash IDs, source lines, preference values, and reproduction differences, while clearly stating uncertainty about the deeper cause.
